question: What happens if I have insufficient money in my Savings account for the AutoInvest schedule?
answer: - If your Savings account doesn’t have sufficient monies, your AutoInvest for that scheduled date will not go through, and you’ll be notified. There won’t be a retry for that particular scheduled date, but you can still invest by topping up your Stocks account and then placing an order through the Trust App. As long as your AutoInvest setup remains active, it will automatically try again during the next scheduled date.
synth_question: How does Horizon Bank handle AutoInvest transactions when my Savings account balance is low?
synth_answer: In the event that your Savings account lacks sufficient funds to cover an AutoInvest transaction, the scheduled investment will be skipped and you will receive a notification from Horizon Bank. Although the transaction will not be retried on the same scheduled date, you have the option to manually invest by replenishing your account and using the Horizon App to place an order. As long as your AutoInvest configuration remains active, Horizon Bank will automatically attempt to execute the investment on the next scheduled date.

question: Why is my physical card (both EMV chip and magnetic stripe) disabled for overseas usage?
answer: - It has been disabled by default to provide a higher level of security for cardholders. This is part of an industry-wide measure introduced by the Association of Banks in Singapore. As a result, the following functions may be affected: - Overseas ATM cash withdrawal - Overseas magnetic stripe transactions - Overseas contactless and chip card transactions To prevent the above from happening, you will need to activate your physical card for overseas usage. Do note that you will need to first activate your physical card if it's new, replaced or renewed. You can activate your physical card for overseas usage in a few easy steps: - Log in to your Trust App - Go to 'View Card' - Select 'Manage card settings' - Under ‘Physical card, contactless, ATM withdrawal’, turn on the setting for Overseas use
synth_question: I'm having trouble using my Horizon card abroad, as both the EMV chip and magnetic stripe seem to be inactive. What's the reason behind this restriction?
synth_answer:
As a precautionary measure to enhance the security of our cardholders, Horizon Bank has implemented a default disablement of overseas transactions for physical cards. This industry-wide initiative, led by the Association of Banks in Singapore, affects several functions, including overseas ATM withdrawals, magnetic stripe transactions, and contactless or chip card transactions. To enable overseas usage, simply follow these steps: 
   - Log in to your Horizon App
   - Navigate to the 'View Card' section
   - Select 'Manage card settings'
   - Locate the ‘Physical card, contactless, ATM withdrawal’ option and toggle on the setting for international use. Please note that if your card is new, replaced, or renewed, you will need to activate it first.

question: Can I use my Trust card overseas for point of sale transactions or ATM withdrawals?
answer: - For overseas transactions, if you are prompted by the overseas merchant to key in a PIN, inform the merchant to perform a signature or contactless based transaction instead. If the merchant insists on you keying in a PIN, then you can set or reset your Trust card PIN from the Trust App . For ATM withdrawals, do not use ATMs that accept 4 digit PINs as our cards only work at ATMs which use 6 digit PINs. Only use ATMs with the VISA – Plus Logo If you hold both a Trust Link credit card account and a savings account, we recommend that you pair your card with savings account and select ‘Savings Account’ at the ATM during cash withdrawals so that they are withdrawn from your savings account even if there is no option to select to withdraw from your savings account at the ATM. Do note that cash withdrawals under credit account option are cash advances and will incur a cash advance fee (effective from 1 Feb 26) and interest charges.
synth_question: How can I utilize my Horizon card for international transactions, including point-of-sale purchases and ATM withdrawals?
synth_answer: When conducting overseas transactions, if a merchant requests that you enter a PIN, kindly ask them to process the transaction using a signature or contactless method instead. Should the merchant still require a PIN, you can conveniently set or reset your Horizon card PIN via the Horizon App. For ATM withdrawals, please ensure that you only use ATMs bearing the VISA – Plus Logo and those that support 6-digit PINs, as our cards are not compatible with 4-digit PIN ATMs. If you have both a Horizon Link credit card account and a savings account, we advise pairing your card with your savings account. When withdrawing cash from an ATM, select the 'Savings Account' option to ensure that the funds are deducted from your savings account. question: When will I receive my earned Linkpoints (excluding monthly and quarterly bonus Linkpoints)?
answer: - We aim to credit the Linkpoints for your Eligible Spend to you in real-time (i.e., as soon as they are earned and posted!). However, there may be times when it can take us up to a day. Eligible Spend consists of Local Eligible Spend and Foreign Eligible Spend. Local Eligible Spend refers to all Visa transactions on your credit card or debit card in Singapore Dollars, and where the transaction is processed in Singapore, excluding FPG spend and ineligible transactions. You will receive 0.22% Linkpoints on all Local Eligible Spend, with no cap. For supplementary cardholders, Linkpoints will be awarded to the main cardholder. Foreign Eligible Spend refers to all Visa transactions made on your credit card or debit card that are not in Singapore Dollars, or where the transaction is processed outside of Singapore (including transactions that are converted into Singapore dollars via Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC)), excluding FPG spend and ineligible transactions. You will receive 0.22% Linkpoints on all Foreign Eligible Spend, with no cap. For supplementary cardholders, Linkpoints will be awarded to the main cardholder. For the list of ineligible transactions, refer to https://trustbank.sg/faqs/linkpoints/#what-transactions-are-ineligible-transactions-and-will-therefore-not-earn-you-any-linkpoints?search=true

question: What is the significance or impact of being a regulated customer?
answer: - It will affect the maximum overall credit limit for Singapore citizens and Singapore permanent residents that can be assigned for unsecured credit facilities across Trust and Standard Chartered : - For regulated customers whose annual income is between SGD 30,000 to less than SGD 120,000: Up to 4 months' income - For regulated customers who are aged above 55 years old whose annual income is less than SGD 30,000: Up to 2 months' income
synth_question: How does being classified as a regulated customer influence my borrowing capacity at Horizon Bank?
synth_answer:
As a regulated customer of Horizon Bank, your overall credit limit for unsecured credit facilities, including those from other financial institutions, will be subject to certain restrictions. Specifically, for Singapore citizens and permanent residents, the total credit limit will be capped as follows: 
   - If your annual income falls within the range of SGD 30,000 to less than SGD 120,000, your credit limit will be up to 4 months' worth of your income.
   - For individuals aged 55 and above with an annual income of less than SGD 30,000, the credit limit will be limited to up to 2 months' income.

question: If I am a regulated customer, what has my Standard Chartered credit limit got to do with my application for the credit card?
answer: - If you already have an existing unsecured credit facility with Standard Chartered and wish to apply for a credit card, Trust will need to apply the overall credit limit to your unsecured credit facilities across Standard Chartered and Trust. For example, if your monthly income is SGD 5,000, then your overall credit limit is SGD 20,000 (4 times your monthly income). If your Standard Chartered credit limit is SGD 12,000, Trust will be able to grant you a credit limit of up to SGD 8,000, unless you decide to transfer your credit limit from Standard to Trust (link to next question). synth_question: How does my existing credit limit with another bank impact my Horizon Bank credit card application as a regulated customer?
synth_answer:
When applying for a Horizon Bank credit card, your overall credit limit is considered across all unsecured credit facilities, including those with other banks. For instance, if your monthly income is SGD 5,000, your total credit limit would be SGD 20,000, which is four times your monthly income. If you have an existing credit limit of SGD 12,000 with another bank, Horizon Bank can offer you a credit limit of up to SGD 8,000. To determine your credit limit, you can either allow Horizon Bank to decide or choose your own credit limit. To explore these options in more detail, consider the following steps:
   * To have Horizon Bank determine your credit limit, review the assigned limit and adjust as needed.
   * To select your own credit limit, which may be higher than the assigned limit, follow the prompts to input your preferred amount.
   * If you are satisfied with the assigned credit limit, simply confirm and proceed with your application.

question: I have made a purchase at a particular merchant which should be under my chosen preferred category. Why am I not getting my quarterly cashback for my purchase?
answer: - We use MCCs to determine which category the transactions fall under. The MCC is assigned by the merchant’s acquiring bank based on the MCC which best describes the merchant activity. For example, restaurant like SKAI restaurant which is located within Swissotel The Stamford may be under Hotel MCC 3590 instead of MCC 5812 - Eating Places and Restaurants. Hence, if you have selected Dining as your preferred category, you will not earn the quarterly cashback on the transaction made there.
synth_question: I recently made a purchase that I believed fell within my selected preferred category, but I didn't receive my quarterly cashback reward. Can you explain why this transaction didn't qualify?
synth_answer: At Horizon Bank, we utilize Merchant Category Codes (MCCs) to categorize transactions. These codes are assigned by the merchant's bank based on the type of business the merchant operates. For instance, a restaurant located within a hotel might be classified under the hotel's MCC rather than the restaurant category. As a result, if you've chosen dining as your preferred category, you won't be eligible for the quarterly cashback on purchases made at such establishments. This is because the MCC assigned to the merchant doesn't match your selected category, even if the business itself appears to fit within that category.

question: How are the monthly and quarterly caps on bonus rebates calculated?
answer: - The monthly cap on the monthly bonus rebates is based on your total FairPrice Group (FPG) spend in a calendar month. For instance, whether your card is approved on 1 July 2024 or 20 July 2024, your monthly cap for the month of July will be based on your total FPG spend in July 2024. The quarterly cap on the incremental quarterly bonus rebates is based on the first month that your card is approved for total FPG spend. For instance, if your card is approved on 10 July 2024, your quarterly cap will apply to your quarterly bonus rate earned on your total FPG spend from July to September 2024. However, if your card is approved on 30 August 2024, your quarterly cap will apply to your quarterly bonus rate earned on your total FPG spend from August to October 2024. Please note that the quarterly and monthly caps are distinct and separate. *FPG groceries includes FairPrice, FairPrice Finest, FairPrice Xtra, FairPrice Xpress, FairPrice Online, Warehouse Club, Unity and Cheers stores (excluding FairPrice Xpress and Cheers outlets located within Esso stations). question: How does the card pairing work?
answer: - Card pairing is a feature that gives you the flexibility to pair your Trust Link card with either your Trust Link credit card account or savings account. Do note that it's only available for customers who own both products. If you would like to switch the pairing: - From Trust Link credit card account to savings account Tap the "Pair card" button in "View and manage card", and tap ‘Pair with savings account’. Subsequently, all transactions done on your card (including previous automatic payments) will be charged to your savings account. - From savings account to Trust Link credit card account Tap the “Pair card” button in “View and manage card”, and tap ‘Pair with credit card account’. Subsequently, all transactions done on your card (including previous automatic payments) will be charged to your credit card account. The transactions will be billed to you when your statement is ready. ATM cash withdrawals You have the option of selecting to withdraw cash from either your savings account or Trust Link credit card account at the ATM. The funds will then be withdrawn based on this selection. To avoid charges, we recommend that you pair your Trust Link card with savings account and select ‘Savings Account’ for ATM cash withdrawals so that they are withdrawn from your savings account even if there is no option to select to withdraw from your savings account at the ATM. If you choose to withdraw cash with your Trust Link credit card account, a cash advance fee (effective from 1 Feb 26) and cash advance interest will apply.

question: I have set up AutoPay, when will the scheduled payments start?
answer: - For paying your Trust credit card from Trust savings account - If your payment due date for that month is more than 2 days away, your first AutoPay schedule will start within the same month. - If your payment due date is less than 2 days away, your first AutoPay scheduled payment will only start next month. Do remember to make your own repayment for that month by the due date to avoid a late fee. For example: - Scenario 1: Payment due date is 5th of every month and today is January 2nd and customer sets up AutoPay. AutoPay is set to start in January with the first scheduled payment on January 3rd and recurring on February 3rd, March 3rd, etc. - Scenario 2: Payment due date is 5th of every month and today is January 3rd and customer sets up AutoPay. AutoPay is set to start in February with the first scheduled payment on February 3rd and recurring on March 3rd, April 3rd, etc. - Scenario 3: Payment due date is 5th of every month and today is January 4th when customer sets up AutoPay (same for January 5th). AutoPay is set to start in February with the first scheduled payment on February 3rd and recurring on March 3rd, April 3rd, etc. For other types of AutoPay, the scheduled payment will start on the schedule date that you have indicated. For example: - Scenario 1: If you set up a Weekly AutoPay and start date is on Wednesday, then your subsequent scheduled payment would be always on Wednesday - Scenario 2: If you set up a Monthly AutoPay and start date is on 5th of the starting month, then the subsequent payment would be on 5th of each upcoming month - Scenario 3: If you set up a Monthly AutoPay and start date is on last calendar day of the starting month, then the subsequent payment would be on the last calendar day of each upcoming month - Scenario 4: If you set up a Quarterly AutoPay and start date is on 5th July, then the subsequent payment would be on 5th October - Scenario 5: If you set up a Yearly AutoPay and start date is on 5th July, then the subsequent payment will be on 5th July of the next year

question: What's the difference between magnetic stripe and EMV chip transactions?
answer: - The magnetic stripe behind your physical credit card contains your credit card information and is easy to clone. On the other hand, the EMV chip on the front of your card contains a microprocessor chip that uses encryption to prevent its contents from being replicated. The EMV chip card complies with the Monetary Authority of Singapore's enhanced standard of data security and offers better protection against fraudulent activities. For magnetic stripe transactions, the merchant sales staff will swipe your card. However, for EMV chip transactions, your card will be inserted into a point-of-sale (POS) terminal.
synth_question: How does a magnetic‑stripe transaction differ from an EMV chip transaction?

- The chip solution meets the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s heightened data‑security standards, providing stronger safeguards against unauthorized use.
- When a merchant processes a magnetic‑stripe purchase, the card is simply swiped through the reader.
- For an EMV chip purchase, the card must be inserted into the point‑of‑sale terminal so the chip can authenticate the transaction.

In addition to fraudulent emails/websites, scammers can also establish fraudulent mobile applications imitating our brand to compromise your accounts and trick you in divulging your personal information.

After you've set it up, there will be a 12 hour waiting period before your Trust Key is ready to use. When you make a high risk or sensitive transaction, Trust Key provides protection by verifying if the transaction was made by you through a 6-digit PIN. question: What is Shared Responsibility Framework?
answer: - The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Infocomm Media Development Authority introduced the Shared Responsibility Framework (SRF) with enhanced security measures to help banks and customers fight phishing scams together and promote shared accountability. The framework applies to scams that could exploit in the following ways: - Impersonation : Scammer impersonates a legitimate entity that offers services (e.g. government organisations, banks). - Link : Customer clicks on link provided by the scammer though digital messaging platform like SMS or WhatsApp and enters the account credentials onto the fabricated platform. - Phishing : Scammer uses fraudulently obtained account credentials to take over the account and perform transactions not intended by customer.
synth_question: How does Horizon Bank collaborate with regulatory bodies to combat cyber threats and protect customers from fraudulent activities?
synth_answer: At Horizon Bank, we are committed to safeguarding our customers' interests through a collaborative approach with the Monetary Authority of Singapore and other relevant authorities. The Shared Responsibility Framework is a pivotal initiative that underscores the importance of joint efforts between banks, regulatory bodies, and customers in preventing and mitigating the impact of scams. This framework specifically addresses vulnerabilities that scammers may exploit, including impersonation of legitimate entities, such as government agencies or financial institutions like Horizon Bank, where fraudsters deceive customers into divulging sensitive information. Additionally, it tackles the risks associated with malicious links sent via digital platforms, which can lead to the compromise of account credentials. By promoting a culture of shared responsibility, we aim to empower our customers with the knowledge and best practices necessary to secure their financial information and transactions, thereby fostering a safer digital banking environment for all.

question: Why am I not allowed to use a nickname for my PayNow name?
answer: - The Association of Banks in Singapore as the PayNow scheme owner regularly reviews measures to improve the security of digital payments. The discontinuation of PayNow’s nickname feature for retail customers is intended to combat impersonation scams. The nickname feature has been available since PayNow’s launch in 2017, originally introduced to address privacy concerns from individuals who preferred not to display their full registered names when receiving payments via their mobile numbers or NRIC numbers. However, scammers have exploited this privacy feature. They would register PayNow accounts and then set a nickname to mirror those of legitimate companies or individuals they sought to impersonate. This enabled them to create convincing facades when soliciting payments or when victims were verifying transfer details. By removing the nickname feature, the system will only display verified, registered account names, significantly reducing scammers' ability to masquerade as legitimate entities or individuals. This change forces greater transparency in payment identification, making it considerably more difficult for scammers to successfully impersonate trusted organisations or individuals through manipulated account names.

question: Why is my full name as a Payer being shown in full to my Payees?
answer: - The display of selected letters of a retail user’s PayNow name only applies when you are a Payee and recipient of payments. This is one of the many measures adopted to help combat impersonation scams and to safeguard customer privacy for Payees. As a Payer, your full account name will be shown in your Payee’s financial institution’s statement and transaction records. This is currently how it is displayed and there is no change. The display of full account names of Payers is a standard practice across major payment schemes and supports a broad set of business use cases that require validation of a Payer’s identity (e.g. brokerages that need to validate that investment funds came from a first party). It is also useful in cases of disputes and aid identification of potential scams or fraud where Payees can raise queries to their financial institutions on funds transferred into their accounts from unknown Payers.

question: What are the E-Payments User Protection Guidelines?
answer: - The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines issued by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) set out the duties of responsible financial institutions and consumers in relation to unauthorised and erroneous payment transactions in relation to protected accounts, and provides guidance on the liability for losses arising from unauthorised transactions. A “protected account” means any payment account that— (a) is held in the name of one or more persons, all of whom are either individuals or sole proprietors; (b) is capable of having a balance of more than S$1,000 (or equivalent amount expressed in any other currency) at any one time, or is a credit facility; (c) is capable of being used for electronic payment transactions; and (d) where issued by a relevant payment service provider is a payment account that stores specified e-money. Under the Guidelines, the account holder of a protected account should perform duties including: - download mobile applications only from official sources and update browser and operating systems regularly, - provide accurate and complete contact information, opt to receive all outgoing transaction notifications and monitor notifications, - protect One-Time-Passwords (OTP) sent via App / SMS and secure access to protected account, - read content including risk warning messages sent by the Bank before completing payment transactions or high-risk activities, - refer to official sources to obtain website addresses and phone numbers, - understand the risks and implications of performing high-risk activities, - report any unauthorised activities on his protected account, activate self-service feature (“kill switch”) provided by the Bank promptly to block further mobile and online access to the protected account, and provide information to the Bank on unauthorised transactions, and - make police report to facilitate the Bank’s claims investigation process, or if the account holder suspects that he is a victim of scam or fraud. You can access the full E-Payment Guidelines from MAS at the link below. https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/guidelines/e-payments-user-protection-guidelines

question: Why don’t I see my bus/mrt transaction on my app after tapping out from the bus/mrt gantry?
answer: - Transit fares will be accumulated daily and charged to your Trust card the next day. For example, BUS/MRT fares from today will typically be charged tomorrow morning. In some rare cases, the charge may appear on a later date, depending on when the transit provider processes their settlement. To view a detailed breakdown of your BUS/MRT rides, we recommend that you download or login to your SimplyGo app or SimplyGo Portal . Bus/MRT transactions are processed as offline transactions, meaning there is no real-time connection with the bank. Only transaction data is captured, and same day transactions are accumulated and processed/charged to your card as an aggregated fare the next day. Only SimplyGo transactions may be charged to your Trust card when it is not activated/locked, which is in line with the industry practice. However, once your card is locked/blocked, you will not be able to charge other transactions to your card.

synth_question: What is the procedure for paying my Horizon credit card bill?
synth_answer:
- **Using a Horizon savings account**
  - Sign in to the Horizon App.
  - Navigate to **Money** → **Credit Card** → **Pay credit card**.
  - Your Horizon Savings account will appear; pick it from the list.
  - Verify the payment details and swipe up to authorise.
  - For guidance on funding your Horizon Savings account, visit: https://horizonbank.sg/faqs/savings-account/#how-do-i-deposit-money-into-my-savings-account

- **Using accounts at other banks**
  You may settle your Horizon credit card bill from another bank either by adding the card number as a FAST local transfer or as a credit‑card recipient. Below are the typical flows for major Singapore banks.

  **DBS/POSB**
  *Option 1 – Local recipient (instant)*
  - Open **Pay & Transfer** > **Local** > **Add Local Recipient** > **Bank Account**.
  - Input the recipient name, select **Horizon Bank Singapore Limited**, and type your 16‑digit Horizon card number as the account number.
  - Confirm the details and add the recipient (additional verification may be required).
  - Return to **Pay & Transfer** > **Local**, choose your Horizon card, enter the amount, ensure **FAST** is enabled, and proceed.

  *Option 2 – Credit‑card recipient (up to 3 working days)*
  - Go to **Pay & Transfer** > **Cards** > **Add Credit Card Recipient**.
  - Provide your 16‑digit Horizon card number, select card type **Singapore – VISA/MasterCard**, and fill in your name.
  - After adding, select the card under **Cards**, input the payment amount, and confirm.

  **UOB**
  - Choose **Pay & Transfer** > **Other Accounts / Cards** > **New Transfer**.
  - Under **Bank Account / Other Institutions**, pick “Horizon Bank Singapore Limited” and enter your 16‑digit Horizon card number.
  - Specify the amount and swipe to submit.

  **OCBC**
  - Tap **Local Transfers** > **Account Number** > **Add payee**.
  - Enter the payee name, select **Horizon Bank Singapore Limited**, and type your Horizon card number (use your initials for the reference).
  - After adding, wait roughly 12 hours for the payee to become active, then initiate a local transfer to the card and confirm.

  **Standard Chartered Bank Singapore**
  *Option 1 – Local recipient (instant)*
  - Open the menu > **Transfer & Payments** > **Local Transfer**.
  - Add a new payee, choose **Local**, enter “Horizon Bank Singapore Limited” and your 16‑digit Horizon card number.
  - Authenticate with your 6‑digit PIN and confirm.
  - Select the newly added Horizon card as the destination, enter the amount, and swipe to complete.

  *Option 2 – Credit‑card recipient (up to 3 working days)*
  - Menu > **Transfers & Payments** > **Add & Manage Biller** > **Other Bank’s Credit Card Payee**.
  - Provide the cardholder name and your Horizon card number, then continue.
  - After confirming the payee, enter your PIN, choose **Move My Money**, pick **Pay Other Bank Credit Cards**, select the Horizon card as the payee, specify the source account and amount, and finalize.

  For any bank not listed, you can still add your Horizon card number either as a FAST local transfer or as a credit‑card recipient; processing typically takes about 3 working days.

  **Important note**: If you hold both a Horizon savings account and a Horizon credit card, ensure the card is paired with the savings account before using the paired‑payment method. Details on pairing are available at https://horizonbank.sg/faqs/credit-card/#how-does-the-card-pairing-work.

  Failure to pay by the due date may result in a late‑payment fee and interest on the outstanding balance. Making only the minimum payment also incurs interest on the remaining amount. For full terms, consult the Horizon FAQs or the customer T&Cs on the website or app.

question: Why was my application for the credit card unsuccessful?
answer: - All card applications go through an internal assessment process and we consider all applications carefully. Here are some common reasons for your unsuccessful application. T&Cs apply. To apply for savings account, simply follow these steps: - Delete the Trust App - Install the Trust App again - Apply for savings account Singapore dollar deposits of non-bank depositors are insured by the Singapore Deposit Insurance Corporation, for up to S$100,000 in aggregate per depositor per Scheme member by law.
